headline: OpenAI's First Hardware is a $230 Mini-Keyboard for AI Power Users
reasoning: This topic scores highly due to its immense clickability, stemming from OpenAI's first foray into hardware being a surprisingly niche and expensive product. While its direct practical value is limited to power users, the story has strong mainstream appeal as it signals the future direction of a major tech player and sparks debate. The subject is also perfect for diverse formats like hot takes ('Is this genius or a gimmick?'), explainers, and gadget comparisons, making it an excellent fit for our publication.
summary: OpenAI has launched its first-ever branded hardware, the Codex Micro, a $230 specialized mini-keyboard created in collaboration with Work Louder to help users monitor and interact with AI agents.

source_articles.title: OpenAI's first branded hardware is... a light-up keyboard?
source_articles.excerpt: The Codex Micro is designed to monitor multiple agentic threads at a glance.
